item.title: Nagasaki Sara Udon — Guide
item.description: Sara udon, meaning ‘plate udon’, is Nagasaki’s other great Chinese-influenced noodle dish and the crispy cousin of champon, created by the same Chinatown restaurant. Instead of soup, it serves noodles topped with a thick, glossy, savoury gravy (an) full of stir-fried pork, seafood, cabbage, beansprouts, kamaboko and other vegetables. It comes in two styles: the more famous version uses fine, crunchy deep-fried noodles that crackle and slowly soften as they soak up the sauce, while a second version uses thicker soft noodles like champon’s.
